posts.card_text: Debt settlement, in one sentence: a creditor agrees to accept less than the full balance.
posts.caption:
That is the whole idea. Instead of paying every dollar over many years, a settlement company negotiates with the creditor to close the account for less than what is owed, paid from money set aside over time.

It is not a loan, and it is not the same as doing nothing. It also has real trade-offs: it can affect credit scores, and creditors may keep calling until an account is settled. It fits some situations and not others.

If you want to know whether it could fit yours, the free review on our site takes about a minute.

posts.card_text: Settling a debt is not the same as ignoring it.
posts.caption:
There is a difference between letting accounts go quiet and working through them on purpose.

Ignoring debt means the balance keeps growing with interest and fees, and the calls keep coming. Settling means a plan: money set aside each month, creditors contacted, accounts closed one at a time for an agreed amount.

Neither path is free of consequences. But one of them ends. If you would like to see what a settlement plan might look like for a set of balances, the review on our site is free and takes about a minute.

posts.card_text: A collector calling is not an emergency. Write down the date, the name, and the amount.
posts.caption:
A few things worth knowing before the phone rings again.

A collector must tell you who they are and what the debt is. You can ask for that in writing, and it is reasonable to say nothing else until it arrives. You do not have to agree to a payment on the call. And keeping a simple log of every call, with the date, the caller, and the amount claimed, makes every later conversation easier.

None of this is legal advice. It is just how to stay calm and organized. If you want help sorting out which balances could be settled, the free review on our site is a good first step.

posts.card_text: Can medical bills be included in a settlement? Usually, yes.
posts.caption:
One of the most common questions we get.

Medical bills are unsecured debt, the same category as credit cards, personal loans, and accounts in collections. That is the kind of debt settlement programs work with. Mortgages, car loans, and federal student loans generally cannot be included, because they are secured or backed by the government.

Every situation is different, and settlement is not right for everyone. If you have a mix of balances and want to know which ones could qualify, the free review on our site sorts that out in about a minute.

posts.card_text: Debt is a math problem, not a character flaw.
posts.caption:
A hospital stay, a slow year, a card that covered groceries when something else fell through. Balances add up for ordinary reasons, and carrying them is not a verdict on anyone.

Math problems have steps. Know the total. Know which balances are unsecured. Know what options exist for each. Then pick one and start.

We are here to explain the options in plain language, with no pressure and no obligation. The free review on our site is the first step, and it takes about a minute.
